problems.description: Deletes the entire seeded Auth API baseline (index.ts) and replaces it with an unrelated static-site-generator package (package-lock name 'ssg', deps: commander, markdown-it, gray-matter; new files cli.ts, cache.ts, ssg.test.ts), so the greenfield session does not build on the intended seed — fit with the story baseline is questionable.

44 naming violations across new files (Classes/Interfaces should be PascalCase, Constants should be UPPER_CASE, Functions should be camelCase in cli.ts, cache.ts, ssg.test.ts), consistent with the measured convention score of 0.54.
Cognitive complexity increased by +7 in the new code, despite the modular split reducing code smells by 3.

strengths: Restructures a single 200-line monolith into a modular multi-file layout (+11 files), improving separation of concerns.
Adds a proper ts-jest test configuration and test file rather than shipping untested code.
No new bugs (0), no duplications (0.0%), and net reduction of 3 code smells.
commit_reviews.summary: A clean modularization with no bugs and added tests, but it discards the seeded Auth API in favor of an unrelated SSG package and ships 44 naming-convention violations (score 0.54), making the change architecturally divergent and debt-positive.

problems.description: Mechanical convention score is 0.54 with 44 violations in ssg.test.ts, cache.ts, and cli.ts (constants not UPPER_CASE, functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase) — below the repo's expected bar.
SonarQube cognitive complexity +9, driven by the nested setupTemplateContent helper and multi-level test setup in ssg.test.ts.
All new template tests write fixtures under the shared testDir with parallel-unsafe paths; concurrent test execution could collide on template/content/output files.
The visible diff only covers tests, package.json, and package-lock.json; the actual src implementation (cache.ts, cli.ts) is in the truncated portion and could not be directly reviewed.

strengths: Uses battle-tested handlebars rather than hand-rolling a templating engine.
Comprehensive coverage of the new template engine: default template, custom frontmatter template, layout wrapping, and partials.
Additive, non-breaking change extending the existing build({ contentDir, outputDir, templatesDir }) signature.
SonarQube reports 0 bugs, 0 smells, and 0.0% duplications.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped, idiomatic addition of a handlebars-based template engine with strong test coverage, held back only by a low mechanical convention score (0.54) reflecting naming-style violations in the touched TypeScript files.

problems.description: Jest config switches from ts-jest to @swc/jest but ts-jest remains in dependencies (unused after this change); should be removed to avoid dead dependency and confusion.

Dev-server tests pick ports via random range (4000 + Math.random()*1000) and use no retry/port-guard, risking flaky or colliding CI runs; fixed high ports or an ephemeral port (port 0) would be more robust.
Tests cover HTTP serving and script injection but not the feature's core chokidar file-watch/live-reload WebSocket behavior, leaving the integration seam untested.
Measured convention score 0.54 with 44 violations (PascalCase/camelCase/UPPER_CASE naming rules) in the touched source files, below the repo's expected bar for new code.
New tests import startDevServer/injectLiveReloadScript directly from "../dev-server" while existing tests import build from "../index"; minor inconsistency with the established re-export pattern.

strengths: Dev server + live reload is a well-scoped feature that fits the SSG's purpose and integrates cleanly at session-3 stage.
New functionality ships with dedicated tests (script injection position, HTTP serving, root index.html), matching the existing describe/test structure.
No new SonarQube bugs or smells, cognitive complexity +1 only, and 0.0% duplication.
Jest transform switch to @swc/jest reuses the already-present @swc/jest devDependency rather than adding a new test toolchain.
commit_reviews.summary: A functionally sound and well-tested integration feature with minor debt from a leftover ts-jest dependency, flaky random-port tests, and a low measured convention score.

problems.description: The --config option and its options type are duplicated verbatim across both commander commands in cli.ts; this drift will likely diverge when one command evolves.
html-generator.ts hardcodes the page shell (head, title, date/tags markup) as string literals instead of routing through the project's templates directory, bypassing the existing templating seam.
SonarQube delta shows +1 smell and +16 cognitive complexity, and the AST diff adds +31 imports; the plugin extraction raised structural complexity rather than lowering it.

Mechanical convention score is 0.54 with 44 naming violations, but the cited files (ssg.test.ts, cache.ts) are largely untouched by this diff — score appears to measure the whole codebase, not just this commit's delta. Flagging the discrepancy.

strengths: dev-server.ts is cleanly gutted into a thin re-export and the implementation moves into plugins/dev-server, a genuine improvement in separation of concerns and alignment with a plugin architecture.
New html-generator.ts centralizes page/index HTML output, removing duplicated markup generation from dev-server and index.
Config file support (ssg.config.ts) added consistently to both build and dev commands, keeping the CLI surface symmetric.
Zero new bugs, zero duplication, and module boundaries respect the existing export-from-index pattern.
commit_reviews.summary: A net-positive structural refactor that extracts the dev server into a plugin module and centralizes HTML generation, though it adds config-option duplication, bypasses the templating seam, and carries a pre-existing low convention score the measurements attribute to files this commit did not change.

problems.description: 44 naming-convention violations (convention score 0.54) across new files ssg.test.ts, cache.ts, and cli.ts: classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE, functions not camelCase.
SonarQube delta shows +4 smells and +10 cognitive complexity, suggesting the incremental-build logic (new cache.ts) is more tangled than the existing modules it augments.
Tests hardcode fake timing expectations (stats.timeSavedMs toBe(100)/toBe(150)) with no actual measured timing, making assertions brittle and potentially misleading.
Each test re-scaffolds contentDir/outputDir/templatesDir setup instead of hoisting to a shared beforeEach, duplicating ~20 lines per test across 8 cases.
Uses manual fs.access().then().catch() boolean pattern instead of a cleaner path-exists helper.

strengths: Feature is well-scoped and domain-appropriate for a static site generator: versioned .ssg-cache.json, per-page cache entries, template-change invalidation, clean flag, and non-incremental fallback form a sound design.
Comprehensive test coverage: cache creation, skip-unchanged, partial rebuild, template invalidation, clean rebuild, and stats accuracy are all exercised.
New options (incremental, clean) extend the existing build() API shape rather than breaking it.
Zero bugs and zero duplications introduced per SonarQube.
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a well-tested incremental-build cache feature that fits the SSG architecture, but ships with 44 naming-convention violations (score 0.54), +4 smells, +10 cognitive complexity, and fake hardcoded timing assertions, making it net worse.

compounding_issues: Committing node_modules/ (session 1) and dist/ + new deps' node_modules (session 3) bloated history by ~80k lines; every later session re-committed vendor files, inflating diffs and review surface.

Session 1's inline string-based HTML generation was never removed; after the Handlebars engine (S2) and plugin extraction (S4), the inline generators persisted as a parallel fallback path in html-generator.ts, keeping two rendering systems alive.
Session 5 hardcoded perPageTimeMs = 50 to fabricate 'time saved' stats in the incremental CLI output — a cosmetic shortcut rather than real measurement.
The seed codebase was an unrelated auth API (JWT/SQLite), so session 1 had to discard the entire provided baseline and start from zero, wasting the seed effort.
Incremental build duplicates the full non-incremental page loop instead of sharing one code path, a mild maintainability smell that grew the hot path in index.ts.
key_decisions: Discard the mismatched auth-API seed and rebuild as a greenfield static site generator in session 1 (markdown walker + frontmatter parsing + page/index generation).
Adopt a Handlebars template engine with layouts and partials in session 2, giving the site a theming layer.
Add a live-reload dev server (chokidar file watching + WebSocket injection) in session 3, exposed via a 'serve' CLI command.

Refactor into a lifecycle-hook plugin architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with a per-file pipeline in session 4, decomposing index.ts into plugins/markdown, plugins/template, plugins/dev-server, html-generator.
Add a content-addressed incremental build cache (SHA-256 source + templates hashing) with --incremental/--clean flags and BuildStats in session 5.
Continuously grow the Jest/ts-jest suite (187 → 892 → 1351 lines) covering templates, dev server, and incremental caching.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Session 1 established a clean, well-factored core; session 2 extended it coherently with templating; session 3 integrated a full dev-server experience; session 4 was a disciplined structural refactor that preserved behavior while shrinking index.ts by more than half; session 5 added a genuinely useful cross-cutting incremental-cache feature with the most thorough test coverage of the whole story. The main persistent weakness is repo hygiene (committed vendor/build artifacts) and the lingering dual rendering paths, but these are minor relative to the monotonic gains in modularity, features, and test depth.
story_review.summary: A strongly coherent five-session arc that progressed from greenfield core to a templated, live-reload, plugin-based, incrementally-cached static site generator with ever-growing test coverage, marred only by vendor-artifact commit hygiene and minor duplicated code paths.
